entries.76cb9d524206e9c9c8de3b4161744828a8155aad: <div sID="gen16936" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="60" osisID="Isa.60" sID="Isa.60"/> <div eID="gen16936" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16937" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen16938" type="x-p"/> This whole chapter is all to the same purport, all in the same strain; it is a part of God's covenant with his church, which is spoken of in the <reference osisRef="Isa.59.21">last verse</reference> of the foregoing chapter, and the blessings here promised are the fruits of the word and Spirit there promised. The long continuance of the church, even unto the utmost ages of time, was there promised, and here the large extent of the church, even unto the utmost regions of the earth; and both these tend to the honour of the Redeemer. It is here promised, I. That the church shall be enlightened and shone upon, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.1-Isa.60.2">ver. 1, 2</reference>. II. That it shall be enlarged and great additions made to it, to join in the service of God, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.3-Isa.60.8">ver. 3-8</reference>. III. That the new converts shall be greatly serviceable to the church and to the interests of it, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.9-Isa.60.13">ver. 9-13</reference>. IV. That the church shall be in great honour and reputation among men, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.14-Isa.60.16">ver. 14-16</reference>. V. That it shall enjoy a profound peace and tranquility, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.17-Isa.60.18">ver. 17, 18</reference>. VI. That, the members of it being all righteous, the glory and joy of it shall be everlasting, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.19-Isa.60.22">ver. 19-22</reference>. Now this has some reference to the peaceable and prosperous condition which the Jews were sometimes in after their return out of captivity into their own land; but it certainly looks further, and was to have its full accomplishment in the kingdom of the Messiah, the enlargement of that kingdom by the bringing in of the Gentiles into it, and the spiritual blessings in heavenly things by Christ Jesus with which it should be enriched, and all these earnests of eternal joy and glory.
entries.9b13eff680cf9fe05f69d28ee27527432b1f93ae: <div eID="gen16938" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen16937" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Extension of the Church. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 706.)</title> <div sID="gen16939" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> is risen upon thee. <hi type="super">2</hi> For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee. <hi type="super">3</hi> And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising. <hi type="super">4</hi> Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at <hi type="italic">thy</hi> side. <hi type="super">5</hi> Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee. <hi type="super">6</hi> The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall show forth the praises of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">7</hi> All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee: they shall come up with acceptance on mine altar, and I will glorify the house of my glory. <hi type="super">8</hi> Who <hi type="italic">are</hi> these <hi type="italic">that</hi> fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows? <div eID="gen16939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16940" type="x-p"/> It is here promised that the gospel temple shall be very lightsome and very large. <div eID="gen16940" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16941" type="x-p"/> I. It shall be very lightsome: <hi type="italic">Thy light has come.</hi> When the Jews returned out of captivity they had <hi type="italic">light and gladness, and joy and honour;</hi> they then were made to <hi type="italic">know the Lord</hi> and to <hi type="italic">rejoice in his great goodness;</hi> and upon both accounts their light came. When the Redeemer came to Zion he brought light with him, he himself came to be a light. Now observe, 1. What this light is, and whence it springs: <hi type="italic">The Lord shall arise upon thee</hi> (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.2">v. 2</reference>), <hi type="italic">the glory of the Lord</hi> (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.1">v. 1</reference>) <hi type="italic">shall be seen upon thee.</hi> God is the father and fountain of lights, and it is in his light that we shall see light. As far as we have the knowledge of God in us, and the favour of God towards us, our light has come. When God appears to us, and we have the comfort of his favour, then <hi type="italic">the glory of the Lord rises upon us</hi> as the morning light; when he appears for us, and we have the credit of his favour, when he shows us some token for good and proclaims his favour to us, then his glory is seen upon us, as it was upon Israel in the <hi type="italic">pillar of cloud and fire.</hi> When Christ arose as the sun of righteousness, and in him <hi type="italic">the day-spring from on high visited us,</hi> then <hi type="italic">the glory of the Lord was</hi> seen upon us, the glory <hi type="italic">as of the first-begotten of the Father.</hi> 2. What a foil there shall be to this light: <hi type="italic">Darkness shall cover the earth;</hi> but, though it be gross darkness, darkness that might be felt, like that of Egypt, that shall overspread the people, yet the church, like Goshen, shall have light at the same time. When the case of the nations that have not the gospel shall be very melancholy, those <hi type="italic">dark corners of the earth</hi> being <hi type="italic">full of the habitations of cruelty</hi> to poor souls, the state of the church shall be very pleasant. 3. What is the duty which the rising of this light calls for: "<hi type="italic">Arise, shine;</hi> not only receive this light, and" (as the margin reads it) "<hi type="italic">be enlightened by it,</hi> but reflect this light; <hi type="italic">arise and shine</hi> with rays borrowed from it." The children of light ought to shine as lights in the world. If God's glory be seen upon us to our honour, we ought not only with our lips, but in our lives, to return the praise of it <hi type="italic">to his honour,</hi> <reference osisRef="Matt.5.16">Matt. v. 16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.2.15">Phil. ii. 15</reference>. <div eID="gen16941" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16942" type="x-p"/> II. It shall be very large. When the Jews were settled again in their own land, after their captivity, many of the people of the land joined themselves to them; but it does not appear that there ever was any such numerous accession to them as would answer the fulness of this prophecy; and therefore we must conclude that this looks further, to the bringing of the Gentiles into the gospel church, not their flocking to one particular place, though under that type it is here described. There is no place now that is the centre of the church's unity; but the promise respects their flocking to Christ, and coming by faith, and hope, and holy love, into that society which is incorporated by the charter of his gospel, and of the unity of which he only is the centre—that family which is named from him, <reference osisRef="Eph.3.15">Eph. iii. 15</reference>. The gospel church is expressly called <hi type="italic">Zion</hi> and <hi type="italic">Jerusalem,</hi> and under that notion all believers are said to <hi type="italic">come</hi> to it (<reference osisRef="Heb.12.22">Heb. xii. 22</reference>. <hi type="italic">You have come unto Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem</hi>), which serves for a key to this prophecy, <reference osisRef="Eph.2.19">Eph. ii. 19</reference>. Observe, <div eID="gen16942" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16943" type="x-p"/> 1. What shall invite such multitudes to the church: "They shall <hi type="italic">come to thy light and to the brightness of thy rising,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.60.3">v. 3</reference>. They shall be allured to join themselves to thee," (1.) "By the light that shines upon thee," the light of the glorious gospel, which the churches hold forth, in consequence of which they are called <hi type="italic">golden candlesticks.</hi> This light which discovers so much of God and his good will to man, by which life and immortality are brought to light, this shall invite all the serious well-affected part of mankind to come and join themselves to the church, that they may have the benefit of this light to inform them concerning truth and duty. (2.) "By the light with which thou shinest." The purity and love of the primitive Christians, their heavenly-mindedness, contempt of the world, and patient sufferings, were the brightness of the church's rising, which drew many into it. The beauty of holiness was the powerful attractive by which Christ had a willing people brought to him in <hi type="italic">the day of his power,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.110.3">Ps. cx. 3</reference>. <div eID="gen16943" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16944" type="x-p"/> 2. What multitudes shall come to the church. Great numbers <hi type="italic">shall come, Gentiles</hi> (or <hi type="italic">nations</hi>) <hi type="italic">of those that are saved,</hi> as it is expressed with allusion to this, <reference osisRef="Rev.21.24">Rev. xxi. 24</reference>. <hi type="italic">Nations</hi> shall be <hi type="italic">discipled</hi> (<reference osisRef="Matt.28.19">Matt. xxviii. 19</reference>), and even kings, men of figure, power, and influence, shall be <hi type="italic">added to the church.</hi> They come from all parts (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.4">v. 4</reference>): <hi type="italic">Lift up thy eyes round about, and see</hi> them coming, <hi type="italic">devout men out of every nation under heaven,</hi> <reference osisRef="Acts.2.5">Acts ii. 5</reference>. See how <hi type="italic">white the fields are already to the harvest,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.4.35">John iv. 35</reference>. See them coming in a body, as one man, and with one consent: They <hi type="italic">gather themselves together,</hi> that they may strengthen one another's hands, and encourage one another. <hi type="italic">Come, and let us go,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.2.3">ch. ii. 3</reference>. "They come from the remotest parts: <hi type="italic">They come to thee from far,</hi> having <hi type="italic">heard the report</hi> of thee, as the queen of Sheba, or <hi type="italic">seen thy star in the east,</hi> as the wise men, and they will not be discouraged by the length of the journey from coming to thee. There shall come some of both sexes. Sons and daughters shall come in the most dutiful manner, as thy sons and thy daughters, resolved to be of thy family, to submit to the laws of thy family and put themselves under the tuition of it. They shall come <hi type="italic">to be nursed at thy side,</hi> to have their education with thee from their cradle." The church's children must be nursed at her side, not sent out to be nursed among strangers; there, where alone the unadulterated milk of the word is to be had, must the church's new-born babes be nursed, <hi type="italic">that they may grow thereby,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Pet.2.1-1Pet.2.2">1 Pet. ii. 1, 2</reference>. Those that would enjoy the dignities and privileges of Christ's family must submit to the discipline of it. <div eID="gen16944" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16945" type="x-p"/> 3. What they shall bring with them and what advantage shall accrue to the church by their accession to it. Those that are brought into the church by the grace of God will be sure to bring all they are worth in with them, which with themselves they will devote to the honour and service of God and do good with in their places. (1.) The merchants shall write <hi type="italic">holiness to the Lord</hi> upon their merchandise and their hire, as <reference osisRef="Isa.23.18">ch. xxiii. 18</reference>. "<hi type="italic">The abundance of the sea,</hi> either the wealth that is fetched out of the sea (the fish, the pearls) or that which is imported by sea, <hi type="italic">shall</hi> all <hi type="italic">be converted to thee</hi> and to thy use." The wealth of the rich merchants shall be laid out in works of piety and charity. (2.) The mighty men of the nations shall employ their might in the service of the church: "<hi type="italic">The forces,</hi> or troops, <hi type="italic">of the Gentiles shall come unto thee,</hi> to guard thy coasts, strengthen thy interests, and, if occasion be, to fight thy battles." The forces of the Gentiles had often been against the church, but now they shall be for it; for as God, when he pleases, can, and, when we please him, will, make even <hi type="italic">our enemies to be at peace with us</hi> (<reference osisRef="Prov.16.7">Prov. xvi. 7</reference>), so, when Christ overcomes the strong man armed, he divides his spoils, and makes that to serve his interests which had been used against them, <reference osisRef="Luke.11.22">Luke xi. 22</reference>. (3.) The wealth imported by land-carriage, as well as that by sea, shall be made use of in the service of God and the church (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.6">v. 6</reference>): <hi type="italic">The camels and dromedaries that bring gold and incense</hi> (gold to make the golden altar of and incense and sweet perfumes to burn upon it), <hi type="italic">those of Midian and Sheba,</hi> shall bring the richest commodities of their country, not to trade with, but to honour God with, and not in small quantities, but camel-loads of them. This was in part fulfilled when the <hi type="italic">wise men of the east</hi> (perhaps some of the countries here mentioned), drawn by the brightness of the star, came to Christ, and presented to him treasures of <hi type="italic">gold, frankincense, and myrrh,</hi> <reference osisRef="Matt.2.11">Matt. ii. 11</reference>. (4.) Great numbers of sacrifices shall be brought to God's altar, acceptable sacrifices, and, though brought by Gentiles, they shall find acceptance, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.7">v. 7</reference>. <hi type="italic">Kedar</hi> was famous for flocks, and probably the fattest rams were those of <hi type="italic">Nebaioth;</hi> these shall come up with acceptance on God's altar. God must be served and honoured with what we have, according as he has blessed us, and with the best we have. This was fulfilled when by the decree of Darius the governors beyond the rivers (perhaps of some of these countries) were ordered to furnish the temple at Jerusalem <hi type="italic">with bullocks, rams, and lambs, for the burnt-offering of the God of heaven,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezra.6.9">Ezra vi. 9</reference>. It had a further accomplishment, and we trust will have, in the bringing in of the fulness of the Gentiles to the church, which is called the <hi type="italic">sacrificing</hi> or <hi type="italic">offering up of the Gentiles</hi> unto God, <reference osisRef="Rom.15.16">Rom. xv. 16</reference>. The flocks and rams are precious souls; for they are said to minister to the church, and to come up as living sacrifices, presenting themselves to God by a <hi type="italic">reasonable service</hi> on <hi type="italic">his altar,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rom.12.1">Rom. xii. 1</reference>. <div eID="gen16945" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16946" type="x-p"/> 4. How God shall be honoured by the increase of the church and the accession of such numbers to it. (1.) They shall intend the honour of God's name in it. When they bring their gold and incense it shall not be to show the riches of their country, nor to gain applause to themselves for piety and devotion, but to <hi type="italic">show forth the praises of the Lord,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.60.6">v. 6</reference>. Our greatest services and gifts to the church are not acceptable further than we have an eye to the glory of God in them. And this must be our business in our attendance on public ordinances, to <hi type="italic">give unto the Lord the glory due to his name;</hi> for <hi type="italic">therefore,</hi> as these here, we are called out of darkness into light, that we should <hi type="italic">show forth the praises of him that called us,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Pet.2.9">1 Pet. ii. 9</reference>. (2.) God will advance the honour of his own name by it; so he has said (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.7">v. 7</reference>): <hi type="italic">I will glorify the house of my glory.</hi> The church is the house of God's glory, where he manifests his glory to his people and receives that homage by which they do honour to him. And it is for the glory of this house, and of him that keeps house there, both that the Gentiles shall bring their offerings to it and that they shall be accepted therein. <div eID="gen16946" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16947" type="x-p"/> 5. How the church shall herself be affected with this increase of her numbers, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.5">v. 5</reference>. (1.) She shall be in a transport of joy upon this account: "<hi type="italic">Thou shalt see</hi> and <hi type="italic">flow together</hi>" (or flow to and fro), "as in a pleasing agitation about it, surprised at it, but extremely glad of it." (2.) There shall be a mixture of fear with this joy: "<hi type="italic">Thy heart shall fear,</hi> doubting whether it be lawful to <hi type="italic">go in to the uncircumcised</hi> and <hi type="italic">eat with them.</hi>" Peter was so impressed with this fear that he needed a vision and voice from heaven to help him over it, <reference osisRef="Acts.10.28">Acts x. 28</reference>. But, (3.) "When this fear is conquered thy heart shall be enlarged in holy love, so enlarged that thou shalt have room in it for all the Gentile converts; thou shalt not have such a narrow soul as thou hast had nor affections so confined within the Jewish pale." When God intends the beauty and prosperity of his church he gives this largeness of heart and an extensive charity. (4.) These converts flocking to the church shall be greatly admired (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.8">v. 8</reference>): <hi type="italic">Who are these that fly as a cloud?</hi> Observe, [1.] How the conversion of souls is here described. It is flying to Christ and to his church, for thither we are directed; it is flying like a cloud, though in great multitudes, so as to overspread the heavens, yet with great unanimity, all as one cloud. They shall come with speed, as a cloud flying on the wings of the wind, and come openly, and in the view of all, <hi type="italic">their</hi> very <hi type="italic">enemies beholding them</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.12">Rev. xi. 12</reference>), and yet not able to hinder them. They shall <hi type="italic">fly as doves to their windows,</hi> in great flights, many together; they fly on the wings of the harmless dove, which flies low, denoting their innocency and humility. They fly to Christ, to the church, to the word and ordinances, as doves, by instinct, to their own windows, to their own home; thither they fly for refuge and shelter when they are pursued by the birds of prey, and thither they fly for rest when they have been wandering and are weary, as Noah's dove to the ark. [2.] How the conversion of souls is here admired. It is spoken of with wonder and pleasure: <hi type="italic">Who are these?</hi> We have reason to wonder that so many flock to Christ: when we see them all together we shall wonder whence they all came. And we have reason to admire with pleasure and affection those that do flock to him: <hi type="italic">Who are these?</hi> How excellent, how amiable are they! What a pleasant sight is it to see poor souls hastening to Christ, with a full resolution to abide with him!
entries.7a658117e77efd95961924cf80851ca83930d8cd: <div eID="gen16947" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Enlargement of the Church. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 706.)</title> <div sID="gen16948" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">9</hi> Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far, their silver and their gold with them, unto the name of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he hath glorified thee. <hi type="super">10</hi> And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee. <hi type="super">11</hi> Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that <hi type="italic">men</hi> may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> their kings <hi type="italic">may be</hi> brought. <hi type="super">12</hi> For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, <hi type="italic">those</hi> nations shall be utterly wasted. <hi type="super">13</hi> The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious. <hi type="super">14</hi> The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , The Zion of the Holy One of Israel. <div eID="gen16948" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16949" type="x-p"/> The promises made to the church in the <reference osisRef="Isa.60.1-Isa.60.8">foregoing verses</reference> are here repeated, ratified, and enlarged upon, designed still for the comfort and encouragement of the Jews after their return out of captivity, but certainly looking further, to the enlargement and advancement of the gospel church and the abundance of spiritual blessings with which it shall be enriched. <div eID="gen16949" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16950" type="x-p"/> I. God will be very gracious and propitious to them. We must begin with that promise, because thence all the rest take rise. The sanctuary that was desolate begins to be repaired when God <hi type="italic">causes his face to shine upon it,</hi> <reference osisRef="Dan.9.17">Dan. ix. 17</reference>. All the favour that the people of God find with men is owing to the light of God's countenance and his favour to them (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.10">v. 10</reference>): "All shall now make court to thee, <hi type="italic">for in my wrath I smote thee,</hi> while thou wast in captivity" (and the sufferings of the church, especially by its corruptions, decays, and divisions, against which these promises will be its relief, are sad tokens of God's displeasure), "But now <hi type="italic">in my favour have I had mercy on thee,</hi> and therefore have all this mercy in store for thee." <div eID="gen16950" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16951" type="x-p"/> II. Many shall be brought into the church, even from far countries (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.9">v. 9</reference>): <hi type="italic">Surely the isles shall wait for me,</hi> shall welcome the gospel, and shall attend God with their praises for it and their ready subjection to it. <hi type="italic">The ships of Tarshish,</hi> transport-ships, shall lie ready to carry members from far distant regions to the church, or (which is equivalent) to carry the ministers of the church to remote parts, to preach the gospel and to bring in souls to join themselves to the Lord. Observe, 1. Who are brought—<hi type="italic">thy sons,</hi> that is, such as are designed to be so, those <hi type="italic">children of God that are scattered abroad,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.11.52">John xi. 52</reference>. 2. What they shall bring with them. They live at such a distance that they cannot bring their flocks and their rams; but, like those who lived remote from Jerusalem (who, when they came up to worship at the feast, because they could not bring their tithes in kind, turned them into money), they shall <hi type="italic">bring their silver and gold with them.</hi> Note, When we give up ourselves to God we must with ourselves give up all we have to him. If we honour him with our spirits, we shall honour him with our substance. 3. To whom they shall devote and dedicate themselves and all they are worth—<hi type="italic">to the name of the Lord thy God,</hi> to God as the Lord of all and the church's God and King, even to the <hi type="italic">Holy One of Israel</hi> (whom Israel worships as a Holy One, in the beauty of holiness), <hi type="italic">because he has glorified thee.</hi> Note, The honour God puts upon his church and people should not only engage us to honour them, but invite us to join ourselves to them. <hi type="italic">We will go with you, for God is with you,</hi> <reference osisRef="Zech.8.23">Zech. viii. 23</reference>. <div eID="gen16951" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16952" type="x-p"/> III. Those that come into the church shall be welcome; for so spacious is the holy city that though, <hi type="italic">Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, yet still there is room. "Therefore thy gates shall be open continually</hi> (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.11">v. 11</reference>), not only because thou hast no reason to fear thy enemies, but because thou hast reason to expect thy friends." It is usual with us to leave our doors open, or leave some one ready to open them, all night, if we look for a child or a guest to come in late. Note, Christ is always ready to entertain those that come to him, is never out of the way, nor can they ever come unseasonably; the gate of mercy is always open, night and day, or shall soon be opened to those that knock. Ministers, the door-keepers, must be always ready to admit those that offer themselves to the Lord. God not only keeps a good house in his church, but he keeps open house, that at any time, by the preaching of the word, <hi type="italic">in season and out of season, the forces of the Gentiles,</hi> and the kings or commanders of those forces, <hi type="italic">may be brought</hi> into the church. <hi type="italic">Lift up your heads, O you gates!</hi> and let such welcome guests as these come in. <div eID="gen16952" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16953" type="x-p"/> IV. All that are about the church shall be made in some way or other serviceable to it. Though dominion is far from being founded in men's grace, it is founded in God's; and he that made the inferior creatures useful to man will make the nations of men useful to the church. The earth helped the woman. <hi type="italic">All things are for your sakes.</hi> So here (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.10">v. 10</reference>), "Even <hi type="italic">the sons of strangers,</hi> that have neither knowledge of thee nor kindness for thee, that have always been <hi type="italic">aliens to the commonwealth of Israel,</hi> even they <hi type="italic">shall build up thy wall, and their kings shall</hi> in that and other things <hi type="italic">ministers unto thee</hi> and not think it any disparagement to them to do so." This was fulfilled when the king of Persia, and the governors of the provinces by his order, were aiding and assisting Nehemiah in building the wall about Jerusalem. Rather than Jerusalem's walls shall lie still in ruins, the <hi type="italic">sons of the stranger</hi> shall be raised up to build them. Even those that do not belong to the church may be a protection to it. And the greatest of men should not think it below them to minister to the church, but rejoice that they are in a capacity, and have a heart, to do it any service. Nay, it is the duty of all to do what they can in their places to advance the interests of God's kingdom among men; it is at their peril if they do not; for (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.12">v. 12</reference>), <hi type="italic">The nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish;</hi> not that they must perish by the sword or by human anathemas, or as if this gave any countenance to the using of external force for the propagating of the gospel, or as if men might be compelled by penalties and punishments to come into the church; by no means. But those who will not by faith submit to Jesus Christ, the King of the church, and serve him, shall perish eternally, <reference osisRef="Ps.2.12">Ps. ii. 12</reference>. Those that will not be subject to Christ's golden sceptre, to the government of his word and Spirit, that will not be brought under, or kept in, by the discipline of his family, shall be broken in pieces by his iron rod. <hi type="italic">Bring them forth and slay them before me,</hi> <reference osisRef="Luke.19.27">Luke xix. 27</reference>. Nations of such shall be utterly and eternally wasted, when Christ shall come to take vengeance on those that <hi type="italic">obey not his gospel,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Thess.1.8">2 Thess. i. 8</reference>. <div eID="gen16953" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16954" type="x-p"/> V. There shall be abundance of beauty added to the ordinances of divine worship (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.13">v. 13</reference>): <hi type="italic">The glory of Lebanon,</hi> the strong and stately cedars that grow there, <hi type="italic">shall come unto thee,</hi> as of old to Solomon, when he built the temple (<reference osisRef="2Chr.2.16">2 Chron. ii. 16</reference>), and with them shall be brought other timber, proper for the carved work thereof, which the enemy had broken down, <reference osisRef="Ps.74.5-Ps.74.6">Ps. lxxiv. 5, 6</reference>. The temple, the <hi type="italic">place of God's sanctuary,</hi> shall be not only rebuilt, but beautified. It is the <hi type="italic">place of his feet,</hi> where he rests and resides, <reference osisRef="Ezek.43.7">Ezek. xliii. 7</reference>. The ark is called his <hi type="italic">footstool,</hi> because it was under the mercy-seat, <reference osisRef="Ps.132.7">Ps. cxxxii. 7</reference>. This he will make glorious in the eyes of his people and of all their neighbours. <hi type="italic">The glory of the latter house,</hi> to which this refers, though in many instances inferior, was yet really <hi type="italic">greater than the glory of the former,</hi> because Christ came to that temple, <reference osisRef="Mal.3.1">Mal. iii. 1</reference>. It was likewise <hi type="italic">adorned with goodly stones and gifts</hi> (<reference osisRef="Luke.21.5">Luke xxi. 5</reference>), to which this promise may have some reference; yet so slightly did Christ speak of them there that we must suppose it to have its full accomplishment in the beauties of holiness, and the graces and comforts of the Spirit, with which gospel ordinances are adorned and enriched. <div eID="gen16954" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16955" type="x-p"/> VI. The church shall appear truly great and honourable, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.14">v. 14</reference>. The people of the Jews, after their return out of captivity, by degrees became more considerable, and made a better figure than one would have expected, after they had been so much reduced, and than any of the other nations recovered that had been in like manner humbled by the Chaldeans. It is probable that many of those who had oppressed them in Babylon, when they were themselves driven out by the Persians, made their court to the Jews for shelter and supply and were willing to scrape acquaintance with them. This prophecy is further fulfilled when those that have been enemies to the church are wrought upon by the grace of God to see their error, and come, and join themselves to it: "<hi type="italic">The sons of those that afflicted thee,</hi> if not they themselves, yet their children, shall crouch to thee, shall beg pardon for their folly and beg an interest in thy favour and admission into thy family," <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.36">1 Sam. ii. 36</reference>. A promise like this is made to the church of Philadelphia, <reference osisRef="Rev.3.9">Rev. iii. 9</reference>. And it is intended to be, 1. A mortification to the proud oppressors of the church, that have afflicted her, and despised her, and taken a pleasure in doing so; they shall be brought down; their spirits shall be broken, and their condition shall be so mean and miserable that they shall be glad to be obliged to those whom they have most studied to disoblige. Note, Sooner or later God will pour contempt upon those that put contempt upon his people. 2. An exaltation to the poor oppressed ones of the church; and this is the honour that shall be done to them, they shall have an opportunity of doing good to those who have done evil to them and saving those alive who have afflicted and despised them. It is a pleasure to a good man, and he accounts it an honour, to show mercy to those with whom he has found no mercy. Yet this is not all. "They shall not only become suppliants to thee for their own interest, but they shall give honour to thee: <hi type="italic">They shall call thee, The city of the Lord;</hi> they shall at length be convinced that thou art a favourite of heaven, and the particular care of the divine providence." That city is truly great and honourable, it is strong, it is rich, it is safe, it is beautiful, it is the most desirable place that can be to live in, which is <hi type="italic">the city of the Lord,</hi> which he owns, in which he dwells, in which religion is uppermost. Such a one is Zion; it is the place which God has chosen to put his name there; it is <hi type="italic">the Zion of the Holy One of Israel;</hi> therefore, we may be sure, it is a holy city, else the Holy One of Israel would never be called the patron of it.
entries.8b1813589b62c946cdec34879047474b2ad2f5ca: <div eID="gen16955" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Glory of the Church. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 706.)</title> <div sID="gen16956" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">15</hi> Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through <hi type="italic">thee,</hi> I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations. <hi type="super">16</hi> Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings: and thou shalt know that I the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> <hi type="italic">am</hi> thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob. <hi type="super">17</hi> For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness. <hi type="super">18</hi> Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise. <hi type="super">19</hi> The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. <hi type="super">20</hi> Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended. <hi type="super">21</hi> Thy people also <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. <hi type="super">22</hi> A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> will hasten it in his time. <div eID="gen16956" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16957" type="x-p"/> The happy and glorious state of the church is here further foretold, referring principally and ultimately to the Christian church and the spiritual peace of that, but under the type of that little gleam of outward peace which the Jews sometimes enjoyed after their return out of captivity. This is here spoken of, <div eID="gen16957" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16958" type="x-p"/> I. As compared with what it had been. <hi type="italic">This</hi> made her peace and honour the more pleasant, that her condition had been much otherwise. <div eID="gen16958" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16959" type="x-p"/> 1. She had been despised, but now she should be honoured, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.15-Isa.60.16">v. 15, 16</reference>. Jerusalem had been forsaken and hated, abandoned by her friends, abhorred by her enemies; no man went through that desolate city, but declined it as a rueful spectacle; it was an <hi type="italic">astonishment and a hissing.</hi> But now it shall be made an eternal excellency, being reformed from idolatry and having recovered the tokens of God's favour, and it shall be <hi type="italic">the joy</hi> of good people for <hi type="italic">many generations.</hi> Yet considering how short Jerusalem's excellency was, and how short it came of the vast compass of this promise, we must look for the full accomplishment of it in the perpetual excellencies of the gospel church, far exceeding those of the Old-Testament church, and the glorious privileges and advantages of the Christian religion, which are indeed the joy of many generations. Two things are here spoken of as her excellency and joy, in opposition to her having been forsaken and hated:—(1.) She shall find herself countenanced by her neighbours. The nations, and their kings, that are brought to embrace Christianity, shall lay themselves out for the good of the church, and maintain its interests with the tenderness and affection that the nurse shows to the child at her breasts (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.16">v. 16</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Thou shalt suck the milk of the Gentiles,</hi> not suck their blood (that is not the spirit of the gospel); thou <hi type="italic">shalt suck the breast of kings,</hi> who shall be to thee as nursing fathers." (2.) She shall find herself countenanced by her God: <hi type="italic">"Thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer,</hi> shalt know it by experience; for such a salvation, such a redemption, shall be wrought out for thee as plainly discovers itself to be the work of the Lord, the work of a mighty one, for it is a great salvation, of the <hi type="italic">Mighty One of Jacob,</hi> for it secures the welfare of all those that are Israelites indeed." They before knew the Lord to be their God; now they know him to be their Saviour, their Redeemer. Their Holy One now appears their Mighty One. <div eID="gen16959" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16960" type="x-p"/> 2. She had been impoverished, but now she shall be enriched, and every thing shall be changed for the better with her, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.17">v. 17</reference>. When those who were raised out of the dust are set among princes, instead of brass money in their purses they have gold, and instead of iron vessels in their houses they have silver ones, and other improvements agreeable: so much shall the spiritual glory of the New-Testament church exceed the external pomp and splendour of the Jewish economy, which had no glory in comparison with that which quite excels it, <reference osisRef="2Cor.3.10">2 Cor. iii. 10</reference>. When we had baptism in the room of circumcision, the Lord's supper in the room of the passover, and a gospel ministry in the room of a Levitical priesthood, we had gold instead of brass. Sin turned gold into brass when Rehoboam made brazen shields instead of the golden ones he had pawned; but God's favour, when that returns, will turn brass again into gold. <div eID="gen16960" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16961" type="x-p"/> 3. She had been oppressed by her own princes, which was sadly complained of, not only as her sin, but as her misery (<reference osisRef="Isa.59.14">ch. lix. 14</reference>); but now all the grievances of that kind shall be redressed (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.17">v. 17</reference>): "<hi type="italic">I will make thy officers peace;</hi> men of peace shall be made officers, and shall be indeed justices, not patrons of injustice, and justices of peace, not instruments of trouble and vexation. They shall <hi type="italic">be peace,</hi> that is, they shall sincerely seek thy welfare and by their means thou shalt enjoy good." They shall be <hi type="italic">peace,</hi> for they shall be righteousness; and <hi type="italic">then</hi> the peace is as a river, when the righteousness is as the waves of the sea. Even <hi type="italic">exactors,</hi> whose business it is to demand the public tribute, though they be exact, must not be exacting, but must be just to the subject as well as to the prince, and, according to the instructions John Baptist gave to the publicans must <hi type="italic">exact no more than is appointed them,</hi> <reference osisRef="Luke.3.13">Luke iii. 13</reference>. <div eID="gen16961" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16962" type="x-p"/> 4. She had been insulted by her neighbours, invaded, spoiled, and plundered; but now it shall be so no more (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.18">v. 18</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Violence shall no more be heard in thy land;</hi> neither the threats and triumphs of those that do violence nor the outcries and complaints of those that suffer violence shall again be heard, but every man shall peaceably enjoy his own. There shall be no <hi type="italic">wasting nor destruction,</hi> either of persons of possessions, any where <hi type="italic">within thy borders;</hi> but <hi type="italic">thy walls shall be called salvation</hi> (they shall be safe, and means of safety to thee) <hi type="italic">and thy gates shall be praise,</hi> praise to thee (every one shall commend thee for the good condition they are kept in), and praise to thy God, <hi type="italic">who strengthens the bars of thy gates,</hi>" <reference osisRef="Ps.147.13">Ps. cxlvii. 13</reference>. When God's salvation is upon the walls it is fit that his praises should be in the gates, the places of concourse. <div eID="gen16962" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16963" type="x-p"/> II. As completed in what it shall be. It should seem that in the close of this chapter we are directed to look further yet, as far forward as to the glory and happiness of heaven, under the type and figure of the flourishing state of the church on earth, which yet was never such as to come any thing near to what is here foretold; and several of the images and expressions here made use of we find in the description of the <hi type="italic">new Jerusalem,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.21.23">Rev. xxi. 23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.5">xxii. 5</reference>. As the prophets sometimes insensibly pass from the blessings of the Jewish church to the spiritual blessings of the Christian church, which are eternal, so sometimes they rise from the church militant to the church triumphant, where, and where only, all the promised peace, and joy, and honour will be in perfection. 1. God shall be all in all in the happiness here promised; so he is always to true believers (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.19">v. 19</reference>): <hi type="italic">The sun and the moon shall be no more thy light.</hi> God's people, when they enjoy his favour, and walk in the light of his countenance, make little account of sun and moon, and the other lights of this world, but could walk comfortably in the light of the Lord though they should withdraw their shining. In heaven there shall be no occasion for sun or moon, for it is the inheritance of the saints in light, such light as will swallow up the light of the sun as easily as the sun does that of a candle. "Idolaters worshipped the sun and moon (which some have thought the most ancient and plausible idolatry); but these <hi type="italic">shall be no more thy light,</hi> shall no more be idolized, but the Lord shall be to thee a constant light, both day and night, in the night of adversity as well as in the day of prosperity." Those that make God their only light shall have him their all-sufficient light, their <hi type="italic">sun and shield. Thy God shall be thy glory.</hi> Note, God is the glory of those whose God he is and will be so to eternity. It is their glory that they have him for their God, and they glory in it; it is to them instead of beauty. God's people are, upon <hi type="italic">this</hi> account, an honourable people, that they have an interest in God as their sin covenant. 2. The happiness here promised shall know no change, period, or allay (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.20">v. 20</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Thy sun shall no more go down,</hi> but it shall be eternal day, eternal sunshine, with thee; that shall not be thy sun which is sometimes eclipsed, often clouded, and, though it shine ever so bright, ever so warm, will certainly set and leave thee in the dark, in the cold, in a few hours; but <hi type="italic">he</hi> shall be a sun, a fountain of light to thee, who is himself the <hi type="italic">Father of all lights,</hi> with whom there is <hi type="italic">no variableness,</hi> nor <hi type="italic">shadow of turning,</hi>" <reference osisRef="Jas.1.17">James i. 17</reference>. We read of the sun's standing still once, and not hasting to go down for the space of a day, and it was a glorious day, never was the like; but what was that to the day that shall never have a night? Or, if it had, it should be a light night; for <hi type="italic">neither shall thy moon withdraw itself;</hi> it shall never wane, shall never change, but be always at the full. The comforts and joys that are in heaven, the glories provided for the soul, as the light of the sun, and those prepared for the glorified body too, as the light of the moon, shall never know the least cessation or interruption; how should they when <hi type="italic">the Lord shall</hi> himself <hi type="italic">be thy everlasting light</hi>—a light which never wastes nor can ever be extinguished? <hi type="italic">And the days of thy mourning shall be ended,</hi> so as never to return; for <hi type="italic">all tears shall be wiped away,</hi> and the fountains of them, sin and affliction, dried up, so that <hi type="italic">sorrow and sighing shall flee away</hi> for ever. 3. Those that are entitled to this happiness, being duly prepared and qualified for it, shall never be put out of the possession of it (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.21">v. 21</reference>): <hi type="italic">Thy people,</hi> that shall inhabit this New Jerusalem, <hi type="italic">shall all be righteous,</hi> all justified by the righteousness of the Messiah, all sanctified by his Spirit; all that people, that Jerusalem, must be righteous, must have that <hi type="italic">holiness without which no man shall see the Lord.</hi> They are all righteous, for we know that <hi type="italic">the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God.</hi> There are no people on earth that are all righteous; there is a mixture of some bad in the best societies on this side heaven; but there are no mixtures there. They shall be <hi type="italic">all righteous,</hi> that is, they shall be entirely righteous; as there shall be none corrupt among them, so there shall be no corruption in them; the <hi type="italic">spirits of just men</hi> shall there be <hi type="italic">made perfect.</hi> And they shall be <hi type="italic">all the righteous</hi> together who shall replenish the New Jerusalem; it is called the <hi type="italic">congregation of the righteous,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.1.5">Ps. i. 5</reference>. And, because they are <hi type="italic">all righteous,</hi> therefore <hi type="italic">they shall inherit the land for ever,</hi> for nothing but sin can turn them out of it. The perfection of the saints' holiness secures the perpetuity of their happiness. 4. The glory of the church shall redound to the honour of the church's God: "They shall appear to be the <hi type="italic">branch of my planting, the work of my hands,</hi> and I will own them as such." It was by the grace of God that they were designed to this happiness; they are <hi type="italic">the branch of his planting,</hi> or of his plantations; he broke them off from the wild olive and grafted them into the good olive, transplanted them out of the field, when they were as tender branches, into his nursery, that, being now planted in his <hi type="italic">garden on earth,</hi> they might shortly be removed to his <hi type="italic">paradise in heaven.</hi> It was by his grace likewise that they were prepared and fitted for this happiness; they <hi type="italic">are the work of his hands</hi> (<reference osisRef="Eph.2.10">Eph. ii. 10</reference>), are <hi type="italic">wrought to the self-same thing,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.5">2 Cor. v. 5</reference>. It is a work of time, and, when it shall be finished, will appear a work of wonder; and God will be glorified, who began it, and carried it on; for the Lord Jesus will then be <hi type="italic">admired in all those that believe.</hi> God will glorify himself in glorifying his chosen. 5. They will appear the more glorious, and God will be the more glorified in them, if we compare what they are with what they were, the happiness they have arrived at with the smallness of their beginnings (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.22">v. 22</reference>): "<hi type="italic">A little one shall become a thousand and a small one a strong nation.</hi>" The captives that returned out of Babylon strangely multiplied, and became a strong nation. The Christian church was a little one, a very small one at first—the number of their names was once but 120; yet it became a thousand. The stone cut out of the mountain without hands swelled so as to fill the earth. The triumphant church, and every glorified saint, will be a thousand out of a little one, a strong nation out of a small one. The grace and peace of the saints were at first like a <hi type="italic">grain of mustard-seed,</hi> but they increase and multiply, and make a little one to become a thousand, the weak to be as David. When they come to heaven, and look back upon the smallness of their beginning, they will wonder how they got thither. And so wonderful is all this promise that it needed the ratification with which it is closed: <hi type="italic">I the Lord will hasten it in his time</hi>—all that is here said relating to the Jewish and Christian church, to the militant and triumphant church, and to every particular believer. (1.) It may seem too difficult to be brought about, and therefore may be despaired of; but the God of almighty power has undertaken it: "<hi type="italic">I the Lord will do it,</hi> who can do it, and who have determined to do it." It will be done by him whose power is irresistible and his purposes unalterable. (2.) It may seem to be delayed and put off so long that we are out of hopes of it; but, as the Lord will do it, so he will <hi type="italic">hasten it,</hi> will do it with all convenient speed; though much time may pass before it is done, no time shall be lost; he will <hi type="italic">hasten it in its time,</hi> in the proper time, in the season wherein it will be beautiful; he will do it in the time appointed by his wisdom, though not in the time prescribed by our folly. And this is really hastening it; for, though it seem to tarry, it does not tarry if it come in God's time, for we are sure that that is the best time, which he that believes will patiently wait for.  <chapter eID="Isa.60"/> <div eID="gen16963" type="x-p"/>

entries.db2cf11f9ff142a67fcb93e0b038b103ad154e8d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9448"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 60</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Isa.60.1-Isa.60.22">Is 60:1-22</reference>. Israel's Glory after Her Affliction.</title> <div sID="gen16414" type="x-p"/> An ode of congratulation to Zion on her restoration at the Lord's second advent to her true position as the mother church from which the Gospel is to be diffused to the whole Gentile world; the first promulgation of the Gospel among the Gentiles, beginning at Jerusalem [Lu 24:47], is an earnest of this. The language is too glorious to apply to anything that as yet has happened.<div eID="gen16414" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16415" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9448"/><hi type="bold">1. Arise--</hi>from the dust in which thou hast been sitting as a mourning female captive (<reference osisRef="Isa.3.26">Is 3:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.52.1">52:1</reference>, 2).<div eID="gen16415" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16416" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shine--</hi>or, "be enlightened; for thy light cometh"; impart to others the spiritual light now given thee (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.3">Is 60:3</reference>). The Margin and Gesenius translate, "Be enlightened"; be resplendent with posterity; imperative for the future indicative, "Thou shalt be enlightened" (<reference osisRef="Isa.58.8">Is 58:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.58.10">10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.5.8">Ep 5:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eph.5.14">14</reference>).<div eID="gen16416" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16417" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">glory of the Lord--</hi>not merely the Shekinah, or cloud of glory, such as rested above the ark in the old dispensation, but the glory of the Lord in person (<reference osisRef="Jer.3.16">Jr 3:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.3.17">17</reference>).<div eID="gen16417" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16418" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">is risen--</hi>as the sun (Mal 4:2; <reference osisRef="Luke.1.78">Lu 1:78</reference>, Margin). <div eID="gen16418" type="x-p"/>

The earth will be afterwards enlightened through Israel (<reference osisRef="Isa.9.2">Is 9:2</reference>).<div eID="gen16419" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16420" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">be seen--</hi>conspicuously: so the Hebrew. <div eID="gen16420" type="x-p"/>

(<reference osisRef="Isa.2.3">Is 2:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.11.10">11:10</reference>; 43:6; 49:22; 66:12).<div eID="gen16421" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16422" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kings--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.49.7">Is 49:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.49.23">23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.52.15">52:15</reference>).<div eID="gen16422" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16423" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy rising--</hi>rather, "thy sun-rising," that is, "to the brightness that riseth upon thee." <div eID="gen16423" type="x-p"/>
entries.3535e72933bd58ef04abf7bf26ba6971a2c61a8a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9451"/><div sID="gen16424" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9451"/><hi type="bold">4. Lift up ... eyes--</hi>Jerusalem is addressed as a female with eyes cast down from grief.<div eID="gen16424" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16425" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all they ... they--</hi>The Gentile peoples come together to bring back the dispersed Hebrews, restore their city, and worship Jehovah with offerings.<div eID="gen16425" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16426" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">nursed at thy side--</hi>rather "carried at thy side." It is the custom in the East to carry the children astride on the hip, with the arms around the body (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.12">Is 66:12</reference>). <div eID="gen16426" type="x-p"/>
entries.19f0e7978f2eaf05afe5aa3b116609c72361ce28: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9452"/><div sID="gen16427" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9452"/><hi type="bold">5. see--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.60.4">Is 60:4</reference>), namely, the bringing back of thy sons.<div eID="gen16427" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16428" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">flow together--</hi>rather, "overflow with joy" [Lowth]; or, from a different Hebrew root, "be bright with joy" [Gesenius] (<reference osisRef="Job.3.4">Job 3:4</reference>).<div eID="gen16428" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16429" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fear--</hi>rather, beat with the agitation of solemn joy at the marvellous sight [Horsley] (<reference osisRef="Jer.33.9">Jr 33:9</reference>).<div eID="gen16429" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16430" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">be enlarged--</hi>swell with delight. Grief, on the contrary, contracts the heart.<div eID="gen16430" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16431" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">abundance of ... sea--</hi>the wealth of the lands beyond the sea, as in Solomon's time, the type of the coming reign of the Prince of peace.<div eID="gen16431" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16432" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">converted--</hi>rather, "be turned," instead of being turned to purposes of sin and idolatry.<div eID="gen16432" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16433" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">forces--</hi>rather, "riches." <div eID="gen16433" type="x-p"/>
entries.ac3a14c00e38ca5d60add36b47576206554fffc1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9453"/><div sID="gen16434" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9453"/><hi type="bold">6. camels--</hi>laden with merchandise; the camel is "the ship of the desert" (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.30.6">Is 30:6</reference>).<div eID="gen16434" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16435" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cover thee--</hi>so many of them shall there be.<div eID="gen16435" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16436" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dromedaries--</hi>They have one hunch on the back, whereas the camel has two: distinguished for swiftness (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.23">Jr 2:23</reference>).<div eID="gen16436" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16437" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Midian--</hi>east of the Elanitic branch of the Red Sea, and stretching northward along Mount Seir. Associated with the Ishmaelites in traffic (<reference osisRef="Gen.37.25">Ge 37:25</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.37.28">28</reference>).<div eID="gen16437" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16438" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Ephah--</hi>part of Midian, east of the Dead Sea. It abounded in camels (<reference osisRef="Judg.6.5">Jud 6:5</reference>).<div eID="gen16438" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16439" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Sheba--</hi>in Arabia-Felix, famed for frankincense and gold (<reference osisRef="Ps.72.15">Psa 72:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.6.20">Jr 6:20</reference>), which they traded in (<reference osisRef="Isa.45.14">Is 45:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.6.19">Job 6:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.27.22">Eze 27:22</reference>). <div eID="gen16439" type="x-p"/>
entries.8f26b87a988f0d450fe869fec56dd5704da9826d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9454"/><div sID="gen16440" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9454"/><hi type="bold">7. Kedar--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.21.16">Is 21:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Song.1.5">So 1:5</reference>), in the south of Arabia-Deserta, or north of Arabia-Petræa; they traded in flocks (<reference osisRef="Ezek.27.21">Eze 27:21</reference>).<div eID="gen16440" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16441" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Nebaioth--</hi>son of Ishmael, as was Kedar. Father of the Nabatheans in Arabia-Petræa.<div eID="gen16441" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16442" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">minister--</hi>by coming up as an acceptable sacrifice.<div eID="gen16442" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16443" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">come up with acceptance--</hi>that is, acceptably. The rams offering themselves voluntarily (<reference osisRef="Ps.68.30">Psa 68:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.12.1">Ro 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.2.5">1Pe 2:5</reference>), without waiting for any other priest, answer to believers strong in faith and lamb-like meekness; and in the white fleece-like robe of sanctity [Vitringa].<div eID="gen16443" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16444" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">house of my glory--</hi>the temple (<reference osisRef="Ezek.41.1-Ezek.41.26">Eze 41:1-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hag.2.7">Hag 2:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.9">9</reference>; Mal 3:1). <div eID="gen16444" type="x-p"/>
entries.7eecdef1efb61082c088c78a81a210e86f0a2a49: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9455"/><div sID="gen16445" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9455"/>8. The prophet, seeing in vision new hosts approaching quickly like a cloud of doves, asks who they are. <div eID="gen16445" type="x-p"/>
entries.b3e68100d2e337a16cdeb1700787f5ca383b1b1d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9456"/><div sID="gen16446" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9456"/>9. (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.42.4">Is 42:4</reference>).<div eID="gen16446" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16447" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Tarshish first--</hi>The ships of Tartessus (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.2.16">Is 2:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.23.1">Is 23:1</reference>, that is, vessels that trade to the most distant regions) will be among the foremost to bring back the scattered Israelites (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.20">Is 66:20</reference>).<div eID="gen16447" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16448" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their silver--</hi>The nations among whom the Jews have been scattered shall help them with their money in returning (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.5-Isa.7.11">Is 60:5-7, 11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.7.16">16</reference>), as was the case at the return from Babylon (<reference osisRef="Ezra.1.4">Ezr 1:4</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Ps.68.30">Psa 68:30</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.68.31">31</reference>).<div eID="gen16448" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16449" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto the name ... to the Holy One--</hi>rather, because of the name--because of the Holy One (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.55.5">Is 55:5</reference>) [Lowth]. <div eID="gen16449" type="x-p"/>
entries.917153e8a38e37284393d9299ef0939f7075e80f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9457"/><div sID="gen16450" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9457"/><hi type="bold">10. kings ... minister unto thee--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Isa.60.7">Is 60:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.49.23">Is 49:23</reference>).<div eID="gen16450" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16451" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in my wrath I smote thee--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.54.7">Is 54:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.54.8">8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.57.17">57:17</reference>). <div eID="gen16451" type="x-p"/>
entries.c5e3bc03566c673b7ee5810a17dd5a787281a696: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9458"/><div sID="gen16452" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9458"/>11. (<reference osisRef="Rev.21.25">Re 21:25</reference>). The gates are ever open to receive new offerings and converts (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.2">Is 26:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.14.27">Ac 14:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.3.8">Re 3:8</reference>). In time of peace the gates of a city are open: so, under the Prince of peace, there shall be no need of barring gates against invaders.<div eID="gen16452" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16453" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">forces--</hi>riches.<div eID="gen16453" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16454" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">be brought--</hi>as willing captives to the truth; or, if not willingly, be bought by judgments to submit to Israel (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.12">Is 60:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.60.14">14</reference>). Gesenius explains it, "may come escorted by a retinue." <div eID="gen16454" type="x-p"/>
entries.d957bb11c55d0c84f59b8c9c16bd98bbed717ce0: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9459"/><div sID="gen16455" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9459"/><hi type="bold">12. For--</hi>the reason which will lead Gentile kings and people to submit themselves; fear of the God in Israel (<reference osisRef="Zech.14.17">Zec 14:17</reference>). <div eID="gen16455" type="x-p"/>
entries.5b350527950f5feb741d97c2164e33bcb822a233: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9460"/><div sID="gen16456" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9460"/><hi type="bold">13. glory--</hi>that is, the trees which adorned Lebanon; emblem of men eminent in natural gifts, devoting all that is in them to the God of Israel (<reference osisRef="Hos.14.5">Ho 14:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.14.6">6</reference>).<div eID="gen16456" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16457" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fir ... pine ... box--</hi>rather, "the cypress ... ilex ... cedar."<div eID="gen16457" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16458" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">place of my sanctuary--</hi>Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Jer.3.17">Jr 3:17</reference>).<div eID="gen16458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16459" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">place of my feet--</hi>no longer the ark (<reference osisRef="Jer.3.16">Jr 3:16</reference>), "the footstool" of Jehovah (<reference osisRef="Ps.99.5">Psa 99:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.132.7">132:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.28.2">1Ch 28:2</reference>); but "the place of His throne, the place of the soles of His feet, where He will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever," in the new temple (<reference osisRef="Ezek.43.7">Eze 43:7</reference>). <div eID="gen16459" type="x-p"/>

entries.b41177f8d7310f1e66139b2c4ab504e7ea95275d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9462"/><div sID="gen16462" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9462"/><hi type="bold">15. forsaken--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.78.60">Psa 78:60</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.78.61">61</reference>).<div eID="gen16462" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16463" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">no man went through thee--</hi>Thy land was so desolate that no traveller, or caravan, passed through thee; true only of Israel, not true of the Church (<reference osisRef="Lam.1.4">La 1:4</reference>).<div eID="gen16463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16464" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">excellency--</hi>glory, that is, for ever honored. <div eID="gen16464" type="x-p"/>

(<reference osisRef="Isa.49.23">Is 49:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.61.6">61:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.66.11">66:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.66.12">12</reference>).<div eID="gen16465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16466" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">know--</hi>by the favors bestowed on thee, and through thee on the Gentiles. <div eID="gen16466" type="x-p"/>
entries.512601e579ce602e3787439d77c9d1b06cd247bd: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9464"/><div sID="gen16467" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9464"/>17. entries.7dbf364e3d2183b9d3538e5775d45df6218e5eca: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9465"/><div sID="gen16470" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9465"/>18. (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.4">Is 2:4</reference>). "Judah," the favored tribe, means "praise." <div eID="gen16471" type="x-p"/>
entries.8d072a34af178de8f564edbebf290b7d830d0b38: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9466"/><div sID="gen16472" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9466"/>19.
